headline: OpenAI's release of hundreds of maths proofs meets only some of the guidelines set by the advisory group of mathematicians that it said it had consulted.
score_reason: A sourced assessment, but it largely repeats the cluster of stories on the same release.
importance_line: Mathematicians who will have to check the proofs are told the release lacked the machine-readable links and explanations the advisers asked for; the verdict is TechCrunch's reading, and the advisory group has not given its own.
summary: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI's release of 719 maths manuscripts this week falls short of guidelines from the nine-member Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, whose first request was to stop testing advanced problems on proprietary models. Only 10 of the manuscripts included the model's chain of thought, and a new paper found at least two mismatches in OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof, adding to the release we carried on 7 Oct 2026 from The Verge.
notes: Read in full. Overlaps C04-01, C04-06, C04-07. TechCrunch's 42% figure not used (conflicts with Yellow.com).
